Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 1–5:

(p-201) (Surat al-Rum (30) is Meccan, except His saying ﴿So glory be to God﴾ and what follows, and its verses are sixty, or fifty-nine verses.)

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

(﴿Alif, Lam, Mim.﴾)

﴿The Romans have been defeated﴾ ﴿in the nearest land﴾, the land of the Arabs nearest to them, because it is the land known to them; or in the nearest part of their land to the Arabs, and the lam (al-lam) is a substitute for the idafa (genitive construction). ﴿But they, after their defeat﴾ is an idafa of the verbal noun to its object, and it was also read "ghalbihim" (their defeat), which is a dialect form like "jalab" and "jalb". ﴿will overcome﴾.

﴿Within a few years﴾. It is related that the Persians raided the Romans and met them at Adhri'at and Busra, and it was said at al-Jazira, which is the nearest land of the Romans to the Persians; so they overcame them. The news reached Mecca, and the polytheists rejoiced and gloated over the Muslims, saying: "You and the Christians are people of a Book, and we and the Persians are unlettered; our brothers have prevailed over your brothers, and we will surely prevail over you." So this was revealed. Abu Bakr said to them: "May God not cool your eyes! By God, the Romans will surely prevail over the Persians within a few years." Ubayy ibn Khalaf said to him: "You have lied. Set between us a term, and I will wager with you on it." So he wagered with him for ten she-camels from each of them, and they fixed the term at three years. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, informed the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: "The 'bid' is what lies between three and nine. So increase the stake and extend the term." So they made it one hundred she-camels, with a term of nine years. Ubayy died of the wound from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) after his return from Uhud. The Romans prevailed over the Persians on the day of Hudaybiyya, and Abu Bakr took the stake from the heirs of Ubayy and brought it to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: "Give it in charity."

The Hanafis cited this as evidence for the validity of void contracts in the territory of war. It was answered that this occurred before the prohibition of gambling. The verse is also among the proofs of prophethood, because it is a report of the unseen. It was also read "ghalabat" with a fatha, and "sayughlabuna" with a damma, meaning that the Romans were overcome in the countryside of Syria, and the Muslims would overcome them. In the ninth year after its revelation, the Muslims raided them and conquered some of their lands; and on this reading the idafa of "ghalab" is to the agent.

﴿To God belongs the command, before and after﴾: before their being victors and during their being vanquished, and after their being vanquished and during their being victors; that is, the command is His at the time they conquered and at the time they are defeated, and neither of these occurs except by His decree. It was also read "min qablu wa min ba'du" without an annexed noun, as if it were said "qablan wa ba'dan", that is, first and last.

﴿And on that day﴾, the day the Romans prevail, ﴿the believers will rejoice﴾.

﴿In the victory of God﴾: whoever has a Book over one who has no Book, because of the reversal of omens in it, the manifestation of the truth of what they had told the polytheists, their winning of the wager, the increase of their certainty, and their steadfastness in their religion. It was also said: "in the victory of God to the believers," by the manifestation of their truthfulness, or by God causing some of their enemies to be allied against others until they perished. ﴿He gives victory to whom He wills﴾, so He grants victory to these at one time and to those at another. ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾: He takes vengeance upon His servants by giving victory over them at times, and He bestows His favor upon them by giving them victory at other times.(p-202)

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 6–7:

﴿The promise of Allah﴾ is a verbal noun (maṣdar) emphasizing itself, because what precedes it carries the meaning of a promise. ﴿Allah does not fail His promise﴾ because lying is impossible for Him, exalted is He. ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ His promise, nor the truthfulness of His promise, due to their ignorance and their failure to reflect.

﴿They know an outward aspect of the worldly life﴾ — that is, what they witness of it and the enjoyment of its adornments. ﴿And they are, of the Hereafter﴾ — which is its ultimate end and its purpose — ﴿heedless﴾: it does not occur to their minds. The second ﴿hum﴾ (they) is either a repetition of the first, or a subject (mubtada') with ﴿heedless﴾ as its predicate, and the sentence is the predicate of the first; on both readings it indicates the firmness of their heedlessness of the Hereafter, which realizes the implication of the preceding sentence, which is substituted for His saying ﴿they do not know﴾, confirming their ignorance and likening them to animals, whose perception of the world is limited to some of its outward aspect. For knowledge of its outward aspect includes knowing its realities, its attributes, its properties, its actions, its causes, how they proceed from it, and how to deal with it. For this reason he used the indefinite ﴿outward﴾. As for its inner aspect, it is a passage to the Hereafter, a means of attaining it, a model of its conditions, and an indication that there is no difference between lacking knowledge and the knowledge that is restricted to the outward aspect of this world.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 8:

﴿Have they not reflected within themselves?﴾ Have they not caused reflection to occur within them? Or: have they not reflected upon the matter of their own selves? For they are closer to them than anything else, and a mirror in which the discerning one sees displayed what is displayed to him in all possible existents, so that there becomes certain to them the power of their Originator to bring them back, like His power to bring them into being. ﴿Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ This is connected to a verb or a knowledge (ʿilm) that is omitted, which the statement indicates. ﴿And for an appointed term﴾ at which they end and after which they do not remain. ﴿And indeed, many of the people are, in the meeting with their Lord﴾ in the meeting with His recompense at the conclusion of the appointed term, or the establishment of the Hour. ﴿are disbelievers﴾ deniers, who reckon that the world is everlasting and that the Hereafter will not be.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 9:

﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen what was the end of those before them?﴾ This is an affirmation of their journeying through the regions of the earth and their looking upon the traces of those destroyed before them. ﴿They were greater than them in strength﴾ like ʿĀd and Thamūd. ﴿And they dug up the earth﴾ and turned over its surface to extract water, to mine minerals, to sow seeds and for other purposes. ﴿And they built it up﴾ and they populated the earth ﴿more than these have built it up﴾, referring to the building up done by the people of Makkah, for they are the people of a valley without cultivation and have no expansion elsewhere. In this there is a mockery of them, in that they are deluded by the world and boast of it, while they are at their weakest state within it, since the whole matter of the world rests upon spreading out in lands, dominating over servants, and disposing of the regions of the earth through various kinds of building, whereas they are weak, compelled to a dwelling that has no benefit. ﴿And their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, that is, with miracles or manifest signs. ﴿So Allah was not to wrong them﴾, that is, He would not do to them what wrongdoers do, destroying them without any offence or prior warning. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾, in that they did what led to their own destruction.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 10:

﴿Then the outcome of those who did evil was the worst [outcome]﴾ That is, then their outcome became the worst outcome, ﴿the worst﴾ or the attribute ( al-suwa )

Thus the apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun, to indicate what necessitated that this be their outcome and that they had brought about deeds like theirs. ( al-suwa ) is the feminine of al-asw'a (the worst), like al-husna (the best), or a verbal noun (masdar) like al-bushra (good news), used as a qualifier. ﴿Because they denied the signs of Allah and used to mock them﴾ This is a causal clause, or an appositive or explanatory apposition to ( al-suwa ), or the predicate of kana, with ( al-suwa ) being a verbal noun of ( asa'u ) or its object in meaning. ﴿Then the outcome of﴾ those who committed the sin was that Allah sealed their hearts until they denied the signs of Allah and mocked them. It is permissible for ( al-suwa ) to be the complement of the verb, with ( an kadhdhabu ) following it and the predicate omitted for vagueness and to convey awe. It is also possible for ( an ) to be explanatory, since when evil is explained as denial and mockery, it implies the meaning of speech. Ibn 'Amir and the Kufans read ( aqibata ) in the accusative, on the basis that the noun is ( al-suwa ) and ( an kadhdhabu ) follows the aforementioned possibilities.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 11–12:

﴿Allah originates creation﴾ — He brings them into being. ﴿Then He repeats it﴾ — He resurrects them. ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾ — for recompense. The shift to the second person (khitab, direct address) is for emphasis on the intended meaning. Abu Bakr, Abu 'Amr and Ruh read it with the ya' (third person, "they will be returned"), in accordance with the original form.

﴿And on the day the Hour arises, the criminals will be dumbfounded﴾ — they will fall silent, bewildered and despairing. It is said: "I debated him and he was made silent (fa-ublisa)" when he fell silent and despaired of being able to argue. From this comes the expression "a she-camel that is mublas", which is one that does not make a sound. It is also read with a fath on the lam, from ablasahu, meaning he silenced him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verses 17–18:

﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning.﴾ ﴿And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth, and in the late afternoon and when you come to midday.﴾ This is a statement in the sense of a command: to declare Allah far above imperfection and to praise Him at these times in which His power becomes manifest and His blessing is renewed. Or it is an indication that what occurs in these times consists of evident signs of His transcendence and of His deserving praise, for those among the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth who have discernment. The specification of glorification to evening and morning is because the traces of power and majesty are more apparent in them. The specification of praise to the late afternoon (al-'ashiyy), which is the end of the day, from "ashá" (the eye grew weak when its light diminished), and to midday (al-zahirah), which is its middle, is because the renewal of blessings is greater in them.

It is permissible that ﴿'ashiyyan﴾ be conjoined to ﴿when you enter the evening﴾, and that ﴿And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth﴾ be a parenthetical clause (i'tiraḍ).

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that the verse comprises the five obligatory prayers: ﴿tumsun﴾ (when you enter the evening) refers to the prayers of Maghrib and 'Isha', ﴿tuṣbihun﴾ (when you enter the morning) to the Fajr prayer, ﴿'ashiyyan﴾ to the 'Asr prayer, and ﴿tuzhirun﴾ (when you come to midday) to the Zuhr prayer. For this reason al-Hasan claimed that it is Medinan, for he used to say: "The obligation in Mecca was two rak'ahs at whatever time they coincided, and its prescribed form of five was only in Medina." But the majority hold that the five were prescribed in Mecca.

It is also related from him, upon him be prayer and peace, that he said: "Whoever would be pleased that he be measured out for with the fullest measure, let him say: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening﴾, the verse."

It is also related from him, upon him be prayer and peace, that he said: "Whoever says when he enters the morning: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening﴾ up to His saying ﴿and thus you will be brought forth﴾, he will attain what he missed during his night; and whoever says it when he enters the evening, he will attain what he missed during his day."

It was also read as ﴿ḥīnan tumsūna﴾ and ﴿ḥīnan tuṣbiḥūna﴾, meaning: the times in which you enter the evening and enter the morning.

﴿He brings forth the living from the dead﴾, such as a human from a drop of semen and a bird from an egg. ﴿And He brings forth the dead from the living﴾, such as a drop of semen and an egg, or it means that death follows life and vice versa. ﴿And He revives the earth﴾ with vegetation. ﴿after its death﴾, i.e., its drying up. ﴿And thus﴾, i.e., like that bringing forth, ﴿you will be brought forth﴾ from your graves, for it too is death following life. Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 23:

﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty.﴾ Your sleep in both times is for the rest of the psychic faculties (al-quwa al-nafsaniyya) and the strengthening of the natural faculties (al-quwa al-tabi'iyya), and for seeking your livelihood in both of them. Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 24:

﴿And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning﴾ — it is governed by an implied "an" (the verbal particle, "that"), as in his saying:

"Unquestioningly, O you who rebuke me for attending battles, and for frequenting pleasures: will you make me immortal?"

Or the verb has the status of a verbal noun (maṣdar), as in their saying: "Hearing about the one who is revived is better than seeing him." Or it is an adjective modifying an omitted noun, whose implied meaning is "a sign by which He shows you the lightning," as in his saying:

"Life is nothing but two moments: one of them I die, and in the other I strive to seek a living, toiling."

"Out of fear of the thunderbolt for the traveler." ﴿And eagerness﴾ for the rain for the resident. Their being in the accusative is on the basis of being a reason (ʿillah) for a verb that the mentioned clause necessitates, for their showing them [the lightning] necessitates their seeing it first. This is either by supposing an omitted genitive construct (muḍāf), such as "the desire of fear and eagerness," or by interpreting fear and eagerness as causing fear and causing eagerness, as in your saying, "I did it in spite of Satan (raghman lil-shaytan)," or as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), like "I spoke to him face to face (shifāhan)."

﴿And He sends down from the sky water﴾ — it is also read with the doubled letter (tashdid). ﴿So He gives life thereby to the earth﴾ — with vegetation. ﴿After its death﴾ — its dryness. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason﴾ — they employ their intellects in deducing its causes and how they come into being, so that the perfect power and wisdom of the Creator becomes manifest to them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verses 25–26:

﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command.﴾ Their standing is by His establishing them and His will that they remain standing in their two appointed places, without any sensible upholder. The expression "by His command" is used to emphasize the perfection of His power and His independence from instruments.

﴿Then, when He calls you with a single call from the earth, behold, you come forth.﴾ It is conjoined to "that the heaven and the earth stand" according to an interpretation of it as a single noun, as if it were said: "And among His signs is the standing of the heavens and the earth by His command, then your coming forth from the graves ﴿when He calls you with a single call﴾, [saying,] 'O dead, come forth.'" The intent is to liken the speed with which this occurs, once His will is connected to it without any delay, hindrance, or need to undertake any labor, to the speed with which a obeyed caller's summons is answered upon his call. The "then" (thumma) is either for the lapse of time or for the magnitude of what is in it. "From the earth" is connected to "called" (da'a), as in your saying: "I called him from the bottom of the valley, and he came up to me," not to "you come forth," because what follows "idha" (when) does not govern what precedes it. The second "idha" is for sudden occurrence (lil-mufaja'a), and for this reason it takes the place of the "fa" (then) in the response to the first.

﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are obedient to Him.﴾ They are submissive to His action upon them and do not resist Him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 27:

﴿And He it is who originates creation, then repeats it﴾ after their destruction. ﴿And it is easier for Him﴾ — repetition (al-i'adah) is easier for Him than origination (al-asl), when measured against your capacity and by analogy with your own origins; otherwise, both are equal for Him. For this reason it has been said that the pronoun (al-ha') refers to "creation" (al-khalq). It has also been said that "easier" (ahwan) carries the sense of "easy" (hayyin), and the masculine form of "huwa" is for "ahwan," or because "repetition" (al-i'adah) carries the sense of "that He repeats" (an yu'id). ﴿And His is the highest description﴾ — al-mathal here means a wondrous attribute of great importance, such as universal power and perfect wisdom. As for the one who interpreted it as the statement "There is no god but Allah," he meant by it the description of divine oneness (al-wahdaniyyah). ﴿The Highest﴾ — the One for whom there is nothing that equals Him or comes near to Him. ﴿In the heavens and the earth﴾ — everything in them describes Him by it, through indication and through speech. ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾ — the Capable, who is not unable to bring into being what is possible and to repeat it. ﴿the Wise﴾ — the One who carries out actions in accordance with the requirements of His wisdom.

﴿He presents to you a parable from your own selves﴾, drawn from their own circumstances, which are the closest matters to you. ﴿Do you have among what your right hands possess﴾, of your slaves, ﴿partners in what We have provided you﴾, of wealth and other things, ﴿so that you are equal in it﴾, so that you and they are partners in it, acting freely with it as you act, even though they are humans like you and it is only lent to you? The first ﴿مِن﴾ (min) is for the beginning of the limit (*li-l-ibtida'*, "to mark the starting point"), the second is partitive (*li-l-tab'id*, "to indicate a part of a whole"), and the third is superfluous, serving to emphasize the interrogation, which takes the place of a negation. ﴿You fear them﴾, that they might arbitrarily take independent control of it.

﴿As you fear one another, your own selves﴾, as free men fear one another. ﴿Thus﴾, like that detailed explanation. ﴿We detail the signs﴾, We make them clear, for detail is what reveals and clarifies meanings. ﴿For a people who use reason﴾, who employ their intellects in contemplating the parables.

﴿Rather, those who did wrong﴾ by associating partners with God ﴿follow their desires without knowledge﴾, being ignorant, with nothing to restrain them, for a knowledgeable person who follows his desire may be deterred by his knowledge. ﴿So who can guide those whom God has led astray?﴾ Who has the power to guide them? ﴿And they have no helpers﴾, who could rescue them from error and protect them from its calamities.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verses 30–31:**

﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth﴾: that is, make it upright for Him, whether you are not turning away from it or turning away from it. This is an image (tamthil) for turning toward it, staying steadfast upon it, and giving it full attention. ﴿The fitrah of Allah﴾: His creation. It is in the accusative (nusiba) either as an incitement (al-igra', a warning or urging to hold fast) or as a verbal noun (al-masdar, مصدر) governed by what the following words indicate. ﴿Upon which He created mankind﴾: He created them upon it, and it is their acceptance of the truth and their capacity to perceive it. Or it means the religion of Islam, for if they were left to what they were created upon, it would lead them to it. It has also been said that it is the covenant taken from Adam and his offspring. ﴿There is no alteration to the creation of Allah﴾: no one is able to change it, or what should not be changed. ﴿That﴾: refers to the religion commanded to be adhered to, or to the fitrah if it is interpreted as the religion. ﴿The upright religion﴾: the straight one in which there is no crookedness. ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾: its straightness, because they do not reflect.

﴿Turning back to Him﴾: returning to Him, from anaba, which means to return again and again. It has also been said that it means being cut off toward Him, from al-nab (the canine tooth), and it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in the implied verb governed by the fitrah of Allah, or from the pronoun in aqim (set), because the verse is addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ) and the community, due to His saying: ﴿Fear Him, establish the prayer, and do not be among the polytheists﴾. However, it was introduced with the address to the Messenger (ﷺ) in honour of him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 32:

﴿Of those who have split up their religion﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "the polytheists." Their splitting refers to their disagreement, concerning what they worship, according to the diversity of their whims (ahwa'). (p-207)

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read (faraqu) instead, meaning they abandoned their religion which they had been commanded to follow. ﴿And they became sects (shiya')﴾, groups, each following its own leader (imam) who led its religion astray. ﴿Every faction, in what they have, rejoicing﴾, delighted, supposing it to be the truth. Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 33–35:

﴿And when harm touches people﴾, i.e., hardship, ﴿they call upon their Lord, turning back to Him﴾, i.e., returning to Him from calling upon others. ﴿Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him﴾, i.e., deliverance from that hardship, ﴿behold, a group of them associate others with their Lord﴾, i.e., a group of them suddenly commit shirk (associating partners) with their Lord, who has granted them well-being.

﴿So that they may deny what We have given them﴾. The lam here is of consequence (lam al-'aqibah, the lam indicating outcome). It was also said that it is the lam of command, in the sense of a threat, due to His saying: ﴿So enjoy yourselves﴾. However, He turned to the third person in it for emphasis. It was also read as "liyatamatta'u" (let them enjoy themselves). ﴿But soon you will know﴾, i.e., the consequence of your enjoyment. It was also read with the yaa' (third person) on the basis that "tamatta'u" is in the past tense.

﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority (sultan)﴾, i.e., a proof. It was also said that it means "one possessing authority," i.e., an angel with them bearing evidence. ﴿So that it speaks﴾, speaking of indication, as in His saying: ﴿This Our Book speaks against you with the truth﴾, or it has spoken. ﴿About what they used to associate with Him﴾, i.e., about their shirk and its validity, or about the matter because of which they associate others with Him in His divinity.

﴿So that they may deny what We have given them﴾. The lam here is of consequence (lam al-'aqibah, the lam indicating outcome). It was also said that it is the lam of command, in the sense of a threat, due to His saying: ﴿So enjoy yourselves﴾. However, He turned to the third person in it for emphasis. It was also read as "liyatamatta'u" (let them enjoy themselves). ﴿But soon you will know﴾, i.e., the consequence of your enjoyment. It was also read with the yaa' (third person) on the basis that "tamatta'u" is in the past tense.

﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority (sultan)﴾, i.e., a proof. It was also said that it means "one possessing authority," i.e., an angel with them bearing evidence. ﴿So that it speaks﴾, speaking of indication, as in His saying: ﴿This Our Book speaks against you with the truth﴾, or it has spoken. ﴿About what they used to associate with Him﴾, i.e., about their shirk and its validity, or about the matter because of which they associate others with Him in His divinity.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 38:

﴿So give to the near of kin his due﴾ such as the maintaining of kinship ties. The Hanafiyyah (the Hanafi school of jurisprudence) used this verse as evidence for the obligation of maintenance (nafaqah) for close relatives within the prohibited degrees (mahram), though it does not actually indicate this.

﴿And to the needy and the wayfarer﴾ [give] what has been prescribed for them from the zakat. The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or to whoever has been granted abundance, and for this reason it is linked to what precedes it by the particle fa' (so). ﴿That is better for those who desire the Face of Allah﴾, meaning His Essence or His direction; that is, they intend by their good deeds Him alone, sincerely, or the direction of drawing near to Him and no other direction. ﴿And those are the successful ones﴾, for they have obtained, through what was granted to them, the enduring bliss.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 39:

﴿And whatever you give as ribā﴾ — an excess that is forbidden in a transaction, or a gift from which one expects a greater return. Ibn Kathir read it with a short vowel (ribā, "giving"), in the sense of "what you have brought of giving ribā." ﴿So that it may increase in the wealth of people﴾ — so that it may grow and multiply in their wealth. ﴿It does not increase with Allah﴾ — it does not grow with Him, and it is not blessed. Nafi' and Ya'qub read (litarbū), meaning "so that you may increase," or "so that you may become people of ribā."

﴿And whatever you give as zakah, seeking the Face of Allah﴾ — seeking by it His Face, sincerely. ﴿Those are the ones who receive multiplied (reward)﴾ — those who possess multiplications of reward. The counterpart of al-mud'if (the one who multiplies) is al-muqwi (the one who strengthens) and al-musir (the one who has wealth and ease), for one who has strength and ease. Or it means: those who have multiplied their reward and their wealth through the blessing of zakah. It is also read with a fathah on the ʿayn, and its deviation from the patterns of correspondence in expression and structure is for emphasis. The shift in address here is for glorification, as if He addressed the angels and the elite of creation, describing their condition; or it is for generality, as if He said: whoever does that, those are the ones who receive multiplied (reward). The returning pronoun is omitted if mā is taken as a relative pronoun, its implied sense being "those who multiply by it," or, "so give it, those are the ones who receive multiplied (reward)."

Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will bring you to life. Is there any of your partners who does anything of that? ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾

He attributed to Him the necessary qualities of divinity and categorically negated them, outright, of what they had taken as partners to Him, from idols and others, emphasizing this with a rhetorical denial, in accordance with what proof and direct observation indicate and on which there is consensus. Then he deduced from that His sanctity above having any partners, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾

It is also permissible for the relative word (al-kalimah al-mawsulah, "the relative pronoun") to be a descriptive modifier (sifah), with the predicate being ﴿Is there any of your partners﴾, and the connecting element (al-rabit) being ﴿of that﴾, because it carries the meaning of "of its actions." The first and second ﴿min﴾ indicate that the ruling is general across the category of partners and actions, and the third ﴿min﴾ is additional, for generalizing the negation. Each of them is independent, serving as emphasis, to render the partners incapable.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with the letter ta' (bi-al-ta', i.e., "tu-shrikūna," addressed in the second person).

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verses 41–42:**

﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea﴾ through things such as drought, scarcity of produce, frequent burning and drowning, the failure of seafarers to profit, the erasure of blessings, and the abundance of harms. Or it means misguidance and injustice. It has been said that by "the sea" is meant the towns of the coasts. It is also recited as *al-buhūr* (البُحُورُ, "the seas," in the plural). ﴿Because of what the hands of people have earned﴾: because of the ill omen of their sins, or because of their earning it. It has been said that corruption appeared on land through Qabil's killing of his brother, and at sea through Julanda, the king of Oman, who used to seize every ship by force. ﴿That He may let them taste some of what they have done﴾: some of its recompense, for its full recompense is in the Hereafter. The *lām* (اللَّامُ, the particle of purpose in Arabic grammar) here indicates either cause (*ʿilla*) or consequence (*ʿāqiba*). Ibn Kathir and Ya'qub recite it as ﴿linudhīqahum﴾ with the *nūn*. ﴿So that they may return﴾ from what they are upon.

﴿Say: Travel through the land and see how was the end of those before﴾ so that you may witness the truth of this and be certain of its veracity.

﴿Most of them were polytheists﴾ is a resumptive sentence (*isti'nāf*, a new sentence that answers an implied question), indicating that the evil end they met was due to the spread and dominance of polytheism among them. Or it means that polytheism was found in most of them, while other sins were found in only a few of them.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verses 44–45:**

﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾, i.e., its consequence (wabal), which is the everlasting Fire. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare [the way]﴾, i.e., they make ready a dwelling in Paradise. The placing of the adverbial phrase (ẓarf) before the verb in both places serves to indicate exclusivity (ikhtiṣāṣ).

﴿That He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds from His bounty﴾. It is a reason (ʿillah) for ﴿yamhadūn﴾ (they prepare), or for ﴿yaṣṣaddaʿūn﴾ (they are divided). The restriction to the reward of the believers serves to indicate that they are the primary intended object, and it is sufficient by way of the implication (faḥwā) of His saying: ﴿Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers﴾, for in it is the affirmation of His hatred toward them and His love toward the believers. The emphasis on the exclusivity of righteousness, which is understood from the omission of their pronoun in favour of explicitly naming them, is a cause for it. ﴿From His bounty﴾ indicates that the granting of reward is pure grace (tafaḍḍul maḥḍ). Interpreting it as "by way of giving" or "an increase upon the reward" is a departure from the apparent meaning.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 46:

﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds﴾ — the north wind (al-shamal), the east wind (al-saba) and the south wind (al-janub), for they are winds of mercy. As for the al-dabur (the west wind), it is a wind of punishment. And from this is his saying, upon him be prayer and peace: "O Allah, make them winds (riyah) and do not make them a single wind (rih)." Ibn Kathir, Hamzah and al-Kisai read ﴿al-riyah﴾ (the winds) with the definite article, with the intention of the genus (al-jins).

﴿bearing good tidings﴾ — of rain.

﴿and that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾ — meaning the benefits that follow from them. It has also been said: the fertility that follows the descent of rain, which is caused by them, or the breeze that accompanies their blowing. The conjunction (al-atf) is upon a deleted cause (illah) indicated by ﴿bearing good tidings﴾, or upon it according to the meaning, or upon ﴿He sends﴾ by supposing a causal verb (fi'l mu'allil) that is indicated by it.

﴿and that the ships may run by His command, and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ — meaning trade by sea.

﴿so that perhaps you may be grateful﴾ — and that you may give thanks for the blessing of Allah the Exalted therein.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 47:

﴿And We certainly sent before you messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs. Then We took vengeance upon those who committed crime﴾ by destruction. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers﴾ is an indication that the retribution was for them and a demonstration of their honour, since He made them deserving, in God's sight, that He should help them. And from him, upon him be prayers and peace, [it is related that he said]: "There is no Muslim man who defends the honour of his brother except that it is incumbent upon God to protect him from the Fire of Hell," then he recited this [verse]. It may also be pause upon "haqqan" (truly/incumbent), taking it as connected with "the retribution" (intiqam).

﴿Allah is He who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and He spreads them across the sky however He wills﴾: spreading them out, sometimes joined together, ﴿in the sky﴾, in its direction, ﴿however He wills﴾, moving or standing still, covering the whole sky or covering it only partly, on one side and not the other, and in other ways. ﴿And makes them fragments﴾: pieces at another time. Ibn ʿĀmir recited it as كِسْفًا *kisfan* with a sukun (the unvocalised form). This may be a lightened form of *kisafan*, or the plural of *kisfa*, or a verbal noun (maṣdar) used as an adjective. ﴿Then you see the rain﴾: the *wadq*, meaning the rain, ﴿coming out from within it﴾ in both states (joined and fragmented). ﴿Then when He causes it to fall upon whomever He wills of His servants﴾: meaning their lands and their territories. ﴿Behold, they rejoice﴾ at the coming of fertility.

﴿And even though before it was sent down upon them﴾: the rain. ﴿Before it﴾: this is a repetition for emphasis and to indicate how long it had been since they had had rain and how firmly their despair had taken hold. It has also been said that the pronoun refers to the rain, or to the clouds, or to the sending (of the winds). ﴿Were certainly despairing﴾: hopeless.

(p-210) ﴿So look at the effects of God's mercy﴾: the effect of the rain on plants, trees and various kinds of fruit. For this reason Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read it in the plural (āthār). ﴿How He brings the earth to life after its death﴾. It is also read with the feminine ta' (tuḥyī), taking as its subject the pronoun referring to mercy (raḥmah). ﴿Surely that﴾, meaning: surely He who is able to give life to the earth after its death, ﴿is the One who gives life to the dead﴾, that is, He is able to bring them back to life, for it is the origination of something like what was in the matter of their bodies of the animal powers, just as the reviving of the earth is the origination of something like what was in it of the vegetative powers. Moreover, it is possible that among the present beings there are those which are made of matter that disintegrated and dispersed from its own kind in some past ages. ﴿And He is powerful over everything﴾, because the relation of His power to all possible things is equal.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on Surah 30, Verse 51:**

﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow﴾. "They saw the trace" or "the crop," since what is meant is implied by what precedes it. It was also said that it refers to the clouds, because when they turn yellow they do not rain. The *lam* in *wa-la'in* is the *lam muwatti'a lil-qasam* (the lam that prepares the way for an oath), which entered upon the conditional particle. The clause ﴿they would have continued to disbelieve after it﴾ is the answer (*jawab*) that stands in the place of the apodosis (*jaza'*), and for this reason it was interpreted in the future tense (*al-istiqbal*).

This verse rebukes the disbelievers for their lack of steadfastness, their failure to reflect, their quick wavering due to their lack of thought, and their poor judgment. Sound reasoning requires that they put their trust in God and turn to Him by seeking forgiveness when the rain is withheld from them, and that they not despair of His mercy. It also requires that they hasten to give thanks and to sustain that thanks through obedience when He bestows His mercy upon them, not being negligent in rejoicing. And it requires that they be patient with His trial when He strikes their crops with yellowing, and that they not be ungrateful for His blessings.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verses 52–53:

﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾, for they are like them, since they have shut their faculties of perception against the truth. ﴿Nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs and flee﴾. He restricted the ruling to this condition so that it would be more impossible, for a deaf person who is facing you, even if he does not hear the speech, grasps something from it through the gestures, [whereas one who has turned away grasps nothing]. Ibn Kathir read "yaa'" with a fatha and raised "al-summu" (the deaf).

﴿Nor can you guide the blind away from their error﴾. He called them blind because they lack the true purpose of sight, or because of the blindness of their hearts. Hamzah alone read "tahdi al-'umya" (you guide the blind). ﴿You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs﴾, for their faith impels them to receive the words and reflect on their meaning. It is also permissible that by "the believer" is meant one who is on the verge of faith. ﴿So they are Muslims﴾, submitting to what you command them.

Allah is the One Who created you from weakness (ﷲ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِن ضَعْفٍ). That is, He originated you weak, and made weakness the foundation of your condition, as in His saying: ﴿And man was created weak﴾. Or it means He created you from a weak origin, which is the sperm-drop (nutfah).

Then He made after weakness strength (ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةً), and that is when you reach puberty (al-hulum), or when the spirit (al-ruh) is attached to your bodies.

Then He made after strength weakness and grey hair (ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ ضَعْفًا وشَيْبَةً), when old age (al-sinn) takes hold of you. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read the ḍād (ض) with a fatḥah throughout all of these occurrences, while the ḍammah is stronger, according to the saying of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I recited it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ‘min ḍaʿfin,’ and he taught me ‘min ḍuʿfin’." Both are dialectal variants, like al-faqr and al-fuqr. The indefinite form with repetition is used because the later state is not the same as the earlier one.

﴿He creates what He wills﴾ of weakness, strength, youth and grey hair (shabbah wa shaybah).

﴿And He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful﴾. For the alternation between different states, while other arrangements were possible, is evidence of knowledge and power.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 55:

﴿And on the day the Hour is established⦗—⦘﴾ al-Qiyamah (the Resurrection) is so named because it is established at the last hour of the worldly life, or because it comes suddenly (p-211).

It became its proper name by dominance, like al-Kawkab (the Star) for al-Zuhrah (Venus). ﴿The criminals will swear that they did not remain⦗ in the world⦘﴾ or in the graves, or in the interval between the annihilation of the world and the resurrection, and the cessation of their punishment. In a hadith: «What lies between the annihilation of the world and the resurrection is forty», and this is open to (the readings of) hours, days, or years. ﴿Except an hour﴾: they belittled the duration of their stay in comparison with the duration of their punishment in the Hereafter, or out of forgetfulness. ﴿Thus﴾: like that diversion from truth and verification. ﴿They were being turned away﴾: they were being diverted in the world.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 56–57:

﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say﴾, [namely] among the angels and mankind. ﴿"You have indeed remained within the Book of God"﴾, i.e., in His knowledge or His decree, or what He has written for you, that is, prescribed; or the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh); or the Qur'an, and this is His saying: ﴿"And behind them is a barrier"﴾. ﴿"until the Day of Resurrection"﴾. By this they refute what the disbelievers said and swore to. ﴿"So this is the Day of Resurrection"﴾, which you denied. ﴿"But you did not know"﴾ that it is true, because of your neglect in reflection. The fa' (so) is the response to an elided conditional clause, whose sense is: "If you were denying the Resurrection, then this is its day," i.e., the falsity of your denial has now become clear.

(﴿So on that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who did wrong﴾.) The Kufans read it with a ya' (yanfa'u, "will not benefit"), because al-Ma'dhira (excuse) has the meaning of al-'Udhr (excuse), or because its feminine gender is not real and a separator has come between them. ﴿"Nor will they be asked to make amends"﴾, i.e., they will not be called to that which would bring about their appeasement (i'tab), that is, the removal of their displeasure (of God) through repentance and obedience, as they were called to it in the world. From the saying: "So-and-so asked me to make amends (istaʿtabani fulan), so I made him amends (fa-aʿtabtuhu)," i.e., he asked me to be pleased, so I pleased him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verses 58–59:

﴿And We have certainly set forth for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾. We described them in it with various kinds of attributes which are, in their strangeness, like examples, such as the attribute of those raised up on the Day of Resurrection: what they say, what is said to them, and that they will not benefit from an excuse or from seeking to be pleased (al-isti'tab). Or it means: We made clear to them, through every kind of example, what would alert them to the Oneness (al-tawhid), the Resurrection, and the truthfulness of the Messenger. ﴿And if you bring them a sign﴾ from the signs of the Qur'an, ﴿those who disbelieve will surely say﴾ — out of their extreme obstinacy and hardness of hearts — ﴿"You are only people of falsehood"﴾, meaning the Messenger and the believers, ﴿"mubtilun"﴾: those who fabricate.

﴿Thus﴾: like that sealing. ﴿God seals upon the hearts of those who do not know﴾: who do not seek knowledge and persist in superstitions they have adopted. For compound ignorance (al-jahl al-murakkab), which is ignorance of one's own ignorance, prevents the perception of truth and necessitates the denial of the one who is right.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 30, verse 60:

﴿So be patient﴾ over their harm. ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah﴾ of your victory and the manifestation of your religion over all other religion ﴿is true﴾; it must be fulfilled. ﴿And let not those who have no certainty﴾ in their denial and their harm of you ﴿make you light-headed﴾, meaning, let them not move you to levity and anxiety. For they are doubters and astray, and it is not strange that they behave in this way.

It is narrated from Ya'qub (al-Hadrami) that he read the nun with a lightened pronunciation (تخفيف النون, *takhfif al-nun*). It is also recited as «وَلا يَسْتَحِقَّنَّكَ» (*wa-la yastahiqqannaka*), meaning: let them not turn you away, so that they would be more deserving of you alongside the believers.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-Rum will have the reward of ten good deeds for each angel who glorified Allah between the heaven and the earth, and he will make up for what he missed in his day and his night."
